meta.what: Curated evidence for the Porter's Five Forces scorer. One fact = one claim + one or more verbatim citations.
meta.authored_by: Claude Code (an LLM agent) chose these facts, wrote the claim text and copied the quotes, in the build session of 2026-10-02. No paid API was used. Code (five_forces.ipynb) checks every quote against cached source text, checks that 'brief' facts really come from brief.json, and drops any fact whose quotes do not verify.

origin_types.brief: Quote already in brief.json (verified in the first project). signal_id + doc_id say where.
origin_types.report_page: New extraction from a page of the same three paywalled reports (cache/pages.jsonl). Quotes <= 25 words.
origin_types.public: New public source fetched by fetch_public.py and cached in public_sources/.

meta.direction: '+' = evidence that the force is STRONG (squeezes profit, pushes the score up). '-' = evidence the force is WEAK (pushes the score down). 'mixed' = cuts both ways; the claim says how.
meta.segment_note: Target segment is US businesses with roughly $2M-$20M revenue buying fractional (part-time) CFO services. Every report figure describes a proxy industry (54161 management consulting, 54121c accounting).

facts.claim: No firm leads: the largest consultancy (Deloitte) holds 5.3% of US management-consulting revenue and everyone outside the top firm shares the other 94.7%.

citations.quote: Deloitte ($22.4bn) 5.3% Other Companies ($397.9bn) 94.7%

facts.claim: The field is a long tail of one-person shops: over 80% of consulting establishments are nonemployers, exactly the profile of a solo fractional CFO.

citations.quote: with over 80.0% of all consultant establishments comprising small, nonemploying companies

facts.claim: A listed mid-market competitor (CBIZ, which bought Marcum's advisory business) describes its own market as highly fragmented and competitive.

citations.quote: The professional services industry is highly fragmented and competitive.

facts.claim: Rivals come from several directions at once: consulting firms, accounting-firm advisory arms, regional business-services firms and independent contractors.

citations.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors > The business services industry is competitive and fragmented
citations.quote: Our principal competitors include financial and management consulting firms, the consulting practices of major accounting firms, local and regional business services companies, independent contractors

facts.claim: Growth is slowing to about 1% a year, so firms grow mainly by taking clients from each other.

citations.quote: Revenue is poised to grow at a CAGR of 1.0% to an estimated $441.6 billion over the next five years

facts.claim: Accounting firms, which already hold the small-business client relationship, are expanding into advisory work because it is more profitable.

citations.quote: the massive profit associated with consulting services will cause companies to expand advisory operations

facts.claim: CPA rules standardize the core service, so providers compete on price and niche expertise.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Barriers to Entry > Differentiation
citations.quote: CPA regulatory requirements create some standardization, causing service providers to compete based on price and expertise in different fields.

facts.claim: Slower business formation made the accounting market more densely competitive and pushed firms into specialized services.

citations.quote: resulting in a more densely competitive market that forces accountants to pivot to specialized service provision.

facts.claim: Offsetting: small firms serving narrow niches face less head-on competition and can hold price.

citations.quote: Competition is kept at bay as they serve niche markets, allowing price stability and even pricing autonomy.

facts.claim: Conflicting signal: First Research says the 50 largest accounting firms hold just under half of revenue, more concentrated than IBISWorld's picture.

citations.quote: the 50 largest US companies account for just less than 50% of revenue

facts.claim: Professional-services costs are mostly fixed in the short run (salaried staff), so idle capacity pushes firms to discount to keep people billable.

citations.quote: a large portion of our operating costs are relatively fixed in the short term

facts.claim: A venture-backed rival publishes an entry price for fractional CFO work, which anchors buyers' price expectations for everyone else.

citations.quote: Starting at $1,750/mo

facts.claim: IBISWorld lists low customer-class concentration as a strength: no customer group dominates.

citations.quote: Strengths Low Capital Requirements Low Customer Class Concentration

facts.claim: The buyer pool is huge and atomized: 36.2 million US small businesses, so no single client can dictate terms to the industry.

citations.section: Q2. How many small businesses are there in the U.S.?
citations.quote: There are 36,207,130 small businesses in the U.S.

facts.claim: Even for a large mid-market provider, the single biggest client is under 2% of revenue.

citations.quote: Our largest client, which is served by the National Practices group, generated approximately 1.7% of our consolidated revenue in 2025.

facts.claim: Switching accounting providers is cheap for the client.

citations.quote: the accounting services space has low switching costs

facts.claim: Engagements are cancellable at will: clients can leave with little notice and no penalty.

citations.section: Forward-looking statements / Item 1A. Risk Factors (client base)
citations.quote: Our clients may terminate our engagements with little or no notice and without penalty

facts.claim: Prospective clients shop on the price of basic services.

citations.section: Executive Insight > Sales/Marketing > Developing Pricing Strategy
citations.quote: Potential clients often compare accounting firms by the price of basic services, adding importance to competitive pricing.

facts.claim: Doing the work in-house (for us: hiring a full-time controller or CFO) is the biggest competitive threat in the client segment that includes small businesses. Treated here as backward integration by the buyer, not as a substitute, so it is not counted twice.

citations.quote: in-house channels remain the largest competitive threat and ate into the segment's revenue stream

facts.claim: IBISWorld's 'high' buyer-power rating is driven by large corporate clients. Our $2M-$20M buyers do not have that leverage individually, so the report's rating overstates buyer power for our segment.

citations.quote: Larger companies wield significant bargaining power, prioritizing consultants' quality of service, brand name and pricing.

facts.claim: Small business owners lean heavily on their accountants for advice, a trust relationship that blunts price shopping once established.

citations.quote: Small business owners often rely heavily on their accounting firms for advice.

facts.claim: Demand is cyclical: a slow economy cuts business needs, which hands buyers leverage in downturns (a retainer is an easy line to cut).

citations.quote: Risk: Slow economy cuts business needs

facts.claim: The key input, credentialed accountants, is scarce: demand has outrun the number of new accountants.

citations.quote: increased demand for accounting services has drastically outpaced the number of new accountants that have begun operating

facts.claim: The pipeline is still shrinking: accounting graduates fell 6.6% in 2023-24 (AICPA 2025 Trends report, as reported by CFO Dive).

citations.quote: The number of U.S. students who graduated with a bachelor's or a master's degree in accounting fell 6.6%

facts.claim: Labor is the biggest cost line, so any talent price increase hits margins directly.

citations.quote: Wages represent the industry's most significant expense category.

facts.claim: BLS projects about 115,300 accountant openings a year, so employers keep competing for the same people.

citations.quote: About 115,300 openings for accountants and auditors are projected each year, on average, over the decade.

origin.note: first quote is also in brief.json (S4, firstresearch_accounting-services); the second is a new extraction from the same page

facts.claim: Senior people carry the client relationships; when one leaves a small firm, revenue goes too. A fractional CFO can walk out and sell directly to the same clients.

citations.section: Challenges, Trends & Opportunities > Dependence on Skilled Personnel
citations.quote: Accounting firms depend heavily on the reputation and expertise of senior partners and the competence of junior accountants.

citations.section: Challenges, Trends & Opportunities > Dependence on Skilled Personnel
citations.quote: The departure of a senior partner in a small firm can greatly impact revenue.

facts.claim: The dominant small-business software supplier is building the finance function into its own product: Intuit's 'Finance Agent' targets forecasting and KPI analysis for mid-market firms, which is CFO work.

citations.quote: Provides a comprehensive approach to the financial management of growing, mid-market businesses with robust reporting, KPI analysis, and scenario planning and forecasting

facts.claim: Offsetting: a pool of part-time professionals, which is the fractional model itself, is IBISWorld's named way to blunt labor supplier power.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Key Success Factors > Be willing to outsource when appropriate
citations.quote: management consultants can mitigate supplier power by maintaining a pool of part-time trained workers available for hire as needed

facts.claim: Easing: accounting enrollment rose 12% and at least 23 states now allow an alternative to the 150-hour CPA rule, so supply should loosen over several years.

citations.quote: the number of accounting students enrolled in colleges and universities last year rose by 12% YoY
23 states have changed their rules to allow for alternative CPA pathways

facts.claim: Startup costs are modest (technology, office, initial marketing); the business is not capital-intensive.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Barriers to Entry > Start-Up Costs
citations.quote: Start-up costs for management consulting include expenses for technology infrastructure, office space and initial marketing campaigns. However, the industry is not capital-intensive

facts.claim: IBISWorld rates both barriers to entry and regulation as low and steady for management consulting, the code that contains our NAICS 541611.

citations.quote: Barriers to Entry Low Steady Regulation and Policy Low Steady

facts.claim: The CPA licence is legally required only for SEC filings and attest work; other accountants get it by choice. Advisory and fractional-CFO work therefore has no licence gate.

citations.section: How to Become One > Licenses, Certifications, and Registrations
citations.quote: Any accountant who files a report with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is required to be a licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA).

citations.section: How to Become One > Licenses, Certifications, and Registrations
citations.quote: Other accountants choose to become a CPA to enhance their job prospects or to gain clients.
Attest services are not permitted to be performed by any individual or entity that is not licensed to do so.

facts.claim: Entry already happens often, and is easiest for specialists serving a narrow market.

citations.quote: New entrants into the accounting space are common due to the limited barriers to entry.
there are lower barriers to entry serving specialized markets and services.

facts.claim: Remote-delivery technology lets small new firms reach clients beyond their city, removing the need for a local office network.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Concentration > Technology supports and incentivizes new entrants
citations.quote: Adopting technologies enabling remote service provision permits smaller firms to grow and expand by accessing a broader client base.

facts.claim: Margins are high enough to attract entrants (EBIT about 17.9% of revenue for accounting, a 2023 figure).

citations.quote: The average profit margin, measured as earnings before interest and taxes, for accounting professionals is high, accounting for an estimated 17.9% of revenue in 2023

facts.claim: Offsetting: standing out takes real investment in brand and a proven track record, which favors incumbents. For a CFO, who is trusted with the client's cash and books, this matters more than the low cash cost of entry.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Barriers to Entry > Differentiation
citations.quote: Establishing a unique value proposition demands significant investment in branding and specialized expertise, which favors incumbent consultants with a proven track record.

facts.claim: Conflicting signal: for firms that practice as CPAs, accounting regulation is rated high and increasing (exam plus 150 credit hours), although IBISWorld still rates barriers to entry as low.

citations.quote: Barriers to Entry Low Increasing Regulation and Policy High Increasing

citations.section: External Environment > Regulation & Policy > CPA requirement
citations.quote: To be designated as a CPA, an individual must pass the Uniform CPA Examination and have 150 credits

facts.claim: ERP and analytics software already replace part of the advisory function by automating processes and giving owners real-time data.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Substitutes > Business software and analytics tools
citations.quote: Advanced business software, including ERP and CRM systems, can replace some management consultant functions by automating processes and providing real-time data insights.

facts.claim: Generative AI offers analysis at close to zero price.

citations.quote: The proliferation of generative AI technology threatens management consultants by efficiently compiling research and offering free analysis

facts.claim: Automation enables do-it-yourself substitutes, especially for the smaller, simpler jobs typical of small businesses.

citations.section: Performance > Current Performance > Automation and AI
citations.quote: it also poses a significant competitive threat via DIY solutions, particularly for smaller tax preparation or statement review cases

facts.claim: Intuit claims its QuickBooks agent automates bookkeeping and reconciliation. That is the base layer a fractional CFO often cleans up first, so this is a vendor claim of substitute performance.

citations.quote: Automates bookkeeping and transaction categorization, and assists in reconciliation, delivering cleaner, more accurate books.

facts.claim: A listed provider tells investors that new technology lets its own clients reduce or bypass its services.

citations.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors > Rapid technological changes
citations.quote: enable our current customers to reduce or bypass the use of our services

facts.claim: Software substitutes do not scale as a robust alternative without a specialist overseeing them, so they complement CFO judgment more than replace it.

citations.section: Competitive Forces > Substitutes > Business software and analytics tools
citations.quote: making them difficult to scale as a robust alternative if specialists are not overseeing their use.

facts.claim: IBISWorld rates the do-it-yourself substitute for accounting as low and steady, because tax complexity keeps clients with professionals.

citations.quote: Do-it-yourself Low Steady
many individuals and larger businesses opt to hire professional accountants due to the complexity of the US tax code

facts.claim: Measured AI use by US businesses is still low (7.6% in Sept 2024-Aug 2025), so the AI substitute is more of a threat for later than a current one.

citations.section: Q4. How are small businesses adopting artificial intelligence?
citations.quote: Between Sept. 2024 and Aug. 2025, 7.6 percent of businesses used artificial intelligence (A.I.).

facts.claim: Tech-enabled substitutes carry their own risk: Bench, a VC-funded bookkeeping platform, shut down without warning, cutting thousands of small businesses off from their books.

citations.quote: Bench touted having more than 35,000 U.S. customers just hours before it was shut down
Bench, which had raised $113 million from high-profile backers such as Shopify and Bain Capital Ventures
